groups.headline: Moog is the strongest long: a record filed quarter with a raised guide, 23% backlog growth and the group's only meaningful FY1 revision (+7.3%). Leidos is the solid secondary — four straight beats, 8-up/0-down revisions and a raised guide at a modest multiple. Woodward is the weakest member: beat sizes have decayed from 31% to 2.9% with flat revisions and the highest P/S in the group, making it the short into its 10/29 print.
groups.tactical: Woodward prints first (10/29) — take the short there and read its aftermarket/aero commentary as the tell for Moog's 11/1 print; add to Moog only on confirmation that the raised guide is tracking, and hold Leidos as the low-multiple carry through its 11/3 print.

best_long.thesis: Moog is the only member with a filed, dated fundamental change: record fiscal Q3 (ended ~2026-06) sales of $1.117B (+15%), adjusted operating margin +280bps, adjusted EPS $3.72 (+60%), full-year guidance raised, and 12-month backlog +23% to $3.3B. FY1 consensus has moved +7.3% in 90 days while peers sit flat. Demand is broad — missile controls, space vehicles, MV-75, commercial aftermarket, and data-center cooling pumps — so the print is not a one-segment story.
best_long.catalyst: Nov 1 print for quarter ending 2026-09-30: first read on whether the raised guide is tracking and whether backlog conversion sustains 15%+ sales growth
best_long.setup: Q4 FY2026 plus FY2027 carry the raised baseline; $3.3B backlog against ~$3.3B trailing revenue gives multi-quarter visibility
best_long.risk: 270bps of last quarter's margin came from one-off IEEPA tariff-claim refunds; if underlying margins ex-claims disappoint, the 32x FY1 multiple compresses hard

groups.headline: RTX is the strongest long setup: four straight beats averaging 14%, the largest last-quarter surprise in the group, 22 analysts up and none down, all at a theme-median multiple. GD is the best secondary — a raised full-year guide on record backlog with 18 upgrades and zero downgrades. The weakest member is AVAV: FY1 estimates cut 20% over 90 days on 14 downgrades against 2 up, a 45x forward P/E, and a beat record of 1-of-4 — the clear short into its 29 September print. — membership deduplicated since the sweep: 1 member(s) now rank under their primary industry (TDG).
groups.tactical: Lead with the AVAV short into 29 Sep — it prints first and its downgrade cycle is the group's cleanest negative. Then build the longs through GE's 14 Oct print, which sets the aftermarket read for NOC (20 Oct), RTX/LMT (23 Oct) and GD (30 Oct); hold HWM and CW for the early-November tail where their raised guides get their first test.

best_long.thesis: RTX combines the group's best beat economics with the least valuation risk: four consecutive beats averaging 14.2%, a 13.7% last-quarter surprise, 22 analysts up and zero down, and a P/E sitting exactly at the theme median. The estimate cycle is still rising (+5.0% FY1 over 90d) and the print only needs to sustain — not re-rate — the growth already priced.

best_long.setup: FY1 growth of 15.1% and FY2 of 8.5% with revisions still rising into the print; the following quarters carry defense backlog conversion and aftermarket pricing.
best_long.risk: Beat sizes decayed from 20.6% to 13.7% over the year; if the next print lands near 5%, the raise cycle stalls at a fully-priced multiple.

groups.headline: ORA is the cleanest long in the group: four straight beats with accelerating surprise sizes, five upward analyst revisions in 30 days, and a filed FY revenue/EBITDA guidance raise into the November print. CWEN is the weak member and the short: its Q2 beat came alongside a trimmed 2026 CAFD outlook, a 1-of-3 beat record, and a downward analyst revision in the last 30 days. In a rising industry, the pair is long ORA against short CWEN around the back-to-back prints on Nov 4-5.
groups.tactical: Short CWEN into its Nov 4 print and hold ORA long through Nov 5, using ORA's result the next day as the read-through on whether renewable operating strength is broad or name-specific; if ORA beats big while CWEN misses under its trimmed CAFD guide, press the pair, and cover CWEN immediately on any guidance restoration.

best_long.thesis: ORA is the only member with an unbroken, accelerating beat record (four of four, surprise growing from 6.9% to 92.7% over four quarters) and the only one that RAISED guidance at its last filing. The Aug 5 exhibit shows 10.6% revenue growth, 20.8% gross profit growth, storage revenue nearly tripling on merchant pricing plus new capacity, and EGS pilots advancing with the ORMEGA100 launch. Five analysts raised FY1 in 30 days with none cutting. The trade is owning that cadence into the Nov 5 print.
best_long.catalyst: Q3 (ending 2026-09-30) on Nov 5: a fifth consecutive beat, ideally with storage revenue still compounding, validates the raised FY revenue/EBITDA guide and keeps the revision cycle running.
best_long.setup: Hold through the print into Q4, where EGS pilot execution and ORMEGA100 commercialization are the next fundamental milestones; FY2 consensus is nearly flat, so beats are the only thing supporting forward estimates.
best_long.risk: Merchant storage pricing mean-reverts and beat sizes collapse back toward the 5-7% historical norm; at ~40x forward earnings with ~1% FY2 growth, a merely in-line quarter is a de-rating event.

groups.headline: BROS is the strongest long in this two-name group: four straight beats, a filed raise to 2026 revenue and EBITDA guidance, and the broadest revision breadth (13 up / 2 down) into a Q3 print that must only sustain, not re-accelerate, its 5-6% comp guide. BJRI is the better secondary long — positive revisions (5 up / 0 down) and a fresh Q2 beat, but its beat sizes have decayed and FY1 growth of just 4.8% gives the print less to clear. Neither name offers a credible short: both have rising estimates, positive filed momentum and no decaying driver the coming print exposes.

groups.headline: NVDA is the strongest long in the group: the only mega-cap with accelerating beat sizes (3.46% to 6.16% across the last four quarters), unanimous upward revisions and a below-median multiple to carry into the quarter ending 2026-09-30. The best secondary long is MPWR, whose FY1 was marked up 13.5% in 30 days on the back of a 10.5% beat with zero downgrades. The weakest member is CRUS: the only name with materially negative revisions (-5.3%), a beat record decaying from 21.9% to 1.4%, and four downgrades in 30 days — the group's clearest short.
groups.tactical: AVGO's Sep 8 print is the group's pivot: it sets the AI read-through that decides how aggressively to press the NVDA, MPWR and MRVL longs into their November prints. Establish the CRUS short ahead of Nov 4 and the QCOM short ahead of Oct 28, but keep the NVDA core long as the anchor position through the print calendar.

best_long.thesis: The group's cleanest fundamental setup: beat sizes have accelerated every quarter (3.46%, 5.32%, 5.54%, 6.16%), FY1 revisions are still rising (+3.7% in 30d, 4 up/0 down), and the filed Q2 FY2027 exhibit shows revenue of $96.2B up 106% with Data Center at $89.0B up 117% — the growth is accelerating into the print, not decaying like AMD or MRVL. Unlike the premium-multiple AI names, NVDA's forward P/E sits below the theme median, so the print does not have to be perfect to hold its bar.
best_long.catalyst: Nov 14 print for the quarter ending 2026-09-30: it reveals whether Data Center growth extends past 100% and whether the forward guide for the January quarter keeps the acceleration intact — the single biggest read-through for the whole group's November prints.
best_long.setup: After the print, FY2 of $13.13 (+45%) gives a second leg: if the September quarter beats by more than June's 6.16% and the guide raises, estimate momentum compounds through the January print. Each of the last four prints has beaten by more than the one before.
best_long.risk: The call breaks if the Data Center guide decelerates or supply constraints cap the January quarter; with revisions already up 3.7% in 30 days, an in-line print underdelivers a fully-priced quarter.

best_short.thesis: The one member the rising industry is leaving behind. FY1 revisions are down 5.3% over 90 days — the whole move in the last 30 days — with 4 analysts down versus 1 up, while every peer's estimates rise. The beat record tells the same story: 19.1%, 21.9%, 10.7%, then 1.39% for the quarter ended 2026-06-30. why_not_cold.reason: The revision lean is tradeable to the upside because AI-driven demand is still accelerating into the next prints: Broadcom's Q3 showed $16.7B AI revenue and a ~$115B FY27 AI target, TSMC reports equipment demand up 90% in six months with ~20 fabs under construction, Lam sees growth extending into 2027, and ADI/MPWR/MCHP/LSCC just printed record quarters with guidance implying further beats — so the coming quarter's order flow and backlog conversions…

groups.headline: CRM is the strongest long in the group: an 80% beat on the July quarter, a filed FY27 revenue-guidance raise and +15% FY1 revisions into a November print that still has room to beat. CDNS is the best secondary — record $8.1B backlog and a raised 19% growth outlook with 10 upgrades and zero down. The weakest member is APP: beats decaying from 10% to 0.4%, FY1 estimates cut on both horizons and 12 of 16 analysts moving down — the group's clearest short.
groups.tactical: ADBE (Sep 12), VEEV (Sep 5) and PATH (Sep 4) print within days and settle the near-term read for application software before the October cluster — use ADBE's result as the AI-disruption tell for the whole group. Build the CRM and CDNS longs ahead of the Oct 28-Nov 26 window, and establish the APP short into the Nov 4 print only after confirming the delay narrative has not cleared in interim commentary.

best_long.thesis: The only member pairing an enormous settled beat (80.4% on the July-2026 quarter) with a filed forward action: FY27 revenue guidance raised to $46.1-46.4B and cRPO growth accelerated to 14% Y/Y constant currency per the August release. FY1 revisions of +15.1% over 90 days are the largest in the group and are still moving (+15.2% over 30 days). The next print reports the September-ending quarter with the raised guide already in hand — a beat-and-raise cadence, not a hope.
best_long.catalyst: Nov 26 print for the quarter ending 2026-09-30: confirms whether the cRPO acceleration converts to revenue and whether the raised FY27 guide gets lifted again.
best_long.setup: Guidance already raised, estimates still chasing upward, and FY2 growth of only 6% leaves the out-year marked too low relative to the current booking trend — successive prints have room to migrate FY2 up.
best_long.risk: The 80% surprise is an outlier against a 35.7% four-quarter average; if Q3 reverts toward the average the optics read as deceleration even on an absolute beat. Position for the guide, not the surprise size.

best_short.thesis: The group's clearest left-behind name inside a rising industry. The beat arc has decayed from 10.1% to 0.4% over four quarters, FY1 consensus has been cut 2.5% over 90 days and 2.0% over 30 days, and 12 of 16 analysts moved down in a month. Reports suggest the June quarter missed revenue expectations with model delays stalling growth — the exact driver the 61% FY1 growth assumption and the 19.5x price-to-sales depend on. Nothing in the filed record supports the growth the multiple still carries.
best_short.catalyst: Nov 4 print for the quarter ending 2026-09-30: the first hard test of whether the model delays are resolved. Another delay or a revenue miss forces the FY2 estimate of 20.28 down from a level the revisions are already sliding toward.
best_short.setup: Estimates are being cut into the print rather than after it, so the surprise bar is lowering — but the FY2 growth of 29.1% is the real target; the September quarter's commentary on the model timeline is what moves it.
best_short.risk: Side matches the revision prior. The risk is asymmetric to the upside: the consumer segment reportedly expanded rapidly and revenue still grew 53% in the June quarter — if the delay narrative clears, the 0.2x-median PEG makes this the most crowded short to cover in the group.

groups.headline: ALGT is the strongest long: a 72.85% beat on the June quarter with filed 2026 view above $6.00 and the group's only genuinely rising FY1 base, though 30-day cuts (-14.35%) temper conviction. VAC is the cleaner secondary long — six up/zero down analysts and a 15.36% beat with revisions still rising into the print. The short side leads this flat-breadth group: TRIP is the weakest member, with FY1 estimates cut ~35% on both horizons and three consecutive misses, ahead of LVS whose June miss (-22.04%) and 14 down-analyst count mark decaying expectations. — membership deduplicated since the sweep: 1 member(s) now rank under their primary industry (TRIP).
groups.tactical: Lead with the TRIP short into the Nov 5 print — it is the group's only one-way-down revision tape and the flat industry breadth gives it no lift; add LVS as the secondary short into the earlier Oct 23 print, sized for hold-normalization risk. Enter the ALGT long after its 30-day estimate reset has fully digested, holding it through the Nov 10 print against the filed >$6.00 view, with VAC as the lower-sized revisions-driven long alongside.

best_long.thesis: ALGT owns the group's only large, fresh beat: Q2 2026 adjusted EPS of $2.19 vs $1.27 consensus (+72.85%), up 78% per the release, with the filed 2026 view above $6.00 against FY1 consensus of $6.48. The 30-day trim (-14.35%, 4 analysts down) has reset the bar below the filed guide, so the Nov 10 Q3 print reports into lowered expectations while the company's own filed outlook is higher — that gap is the trade.

Use any OMC weakness as the read-through to press WBD into 11/5, and hold TKO long through 11/1 as the group's only filed-raise story, trimming if the raised guide is met but not beaten.

The revision tape confirms the filings — FY1 EPS up 4.2% over 90 days and 18.7% over 30 days, 4 analysts up vs 2 down — and the Q2 beat (+23.3%) is the first of the last four, suggesting the record is turning rather than decaying. Premium live content demand is the driver, and the raised guide gives a concrete bar the Q3 print must clear.

best_long.risk: The multiple is the vulnerability: at ~41x forward earnings the print must beat AND ideally raise again — an in-line quarter after a guide raise would compress the multiple sharply. The 1-of-4 beat record means the market has not yet been trained to trust this name.

groups.headline: Medtronic is the strongest long: four straight beats with accelerating surprise sizes, the fastest 30-day revisions in the group, and reports of a raised FY27 guide, all landing at its print in 15 days. Abbott is the solid secondary — a 4/4 beat record and a raised FY26 EPS guide, but flatter 30-day revisions and a longer wait until late October. Neither member offers a credible short in a group with +1.00 breadth and both companies raising guidance; the short side is null.
groups.tactical: Own MDT into its 15-day print as the primary expression, then rotate or add to ABT after MDT's read-through — broad medtech demand strength would support ABT's October quarter — keeping both longs sized off the raised-guidance baseline rather than the beat history.

best_long.thesis: MDT combines the group's best beat trajectory (4/4, avg surprise 2.6% and rising: 3.49%, 1.86%, 0.56%, 4.51%) with the fastest near-term revisions (FY1 +0.35% in 30d) and reports of a raised FY27 outlook on heart-device demand and broad portfolio growth. It prints first, so the market re-marks it before ABT even reports.
best_long.catalyst: The next print (2026-09-17 per packet) reveals whether the reported Q1 FY27 strength and raised guidance extend; a confirm-and-raise print validates the revision uptrend.
best_long.setup: Own into the print; the raised FY27 guide per reports gives a fundamental floor, and FY2 growth of ~7.7% supports continued estimate builds through the following quarters.
best_long.risk: The Sep 1 news flow suggests results may already be public — if the market has fully absorbed the beat and raise, the setup is spent and an in-line follow-up quarter de-rates the ~15.5x FY1 multiple.

leaderboard.summary: Best risk/reward sits in names where large, fresh estimate revisions and decisive last beats land soon: DELL (print in 6 days, +41% revisions) leads, with HLNE, DRH, ALGT and TGT the strongest fuller-horizon longs. On the short side, COIN, AVAV, TRIP and CDE combine steep estimate cuts with recent misses. Overlaps to respect: MOG-A/RTX share the aerospace/defense driver; VICR and FTNT both lean on tech-security/electronics demand; ODFL, NSC, WAB, SAIA, MRTN and ALK all express the same freight-cycle view, so size them as one theme; ANDE/PFGC and DRH/SHO are also single-driver pairs.
